title_en: Japan's 2026 agricultural credit guarantee accounting rule: how guarantee losses may be covered

instruments.number: 令和八年内閣府・農林水産省令第十二号
instruments.name_ja: 農業信用保証保険法施行規則の一部を改正する命令
instruments.name_en: Cabinet Office–MAFF Ordinance No. 12 of 2026 amending the Enforcement Regulation of the Agricultural Credit Guarantee Insurance Act

watch_pages.label: e-Gov current Agricultural Credit Guarantee Insurance Act Enforcement Regulation

quick_take.what_changed: Ordinance No. 12 of 2026 added Article 3-2 to the agricultural credit guarantee insurance enforcement regulation, expressly permitting specified reserves and transfers to cover deficits in designated guarantee-operation accounts.
quick_take.who_is_affected: The accounting rule addresses bodies carrying out guarantee operations under Article 11 items 1–3 of the Agricultural Credit Guarantee Insurance Act; it does not directly amend farm borrowers' eligibility.
quick_take.what_to_do_now: For accounting periods affected from 1 October 2026, check the precise Article 10 reserve and transfer balances and document the statutory order of use before treating a deficit as covered.

paragraphs: Agricultural credit guarantees support financing for farm businesses by allocating certain lending risks through a statutory guarantee and insurance framework. Financial resilience of the guarantee system matters to farmers seeking credit, but the rules governing an institution's accounting reserves are distinct from the contractual criteria for an individual loan or guarantee.

The 2026 change concerns what happens when the accounts for the guarantee operations identified in Article 11 items 1 to 3 show a shortfall. Before the amendment, the enforcement regulation contained no Article 3-2 expressly setting out the drawdown sequence. The new provision adds an accounting mechanism rather than imposing a new lending quota or altering the statutory rights of agricultural borrowers.

MAFF explained in its consultation response that the proposal was intended to secure stable operation of the agricultural credit guarantee insurance system and facilitate agricultural financing. A submission raised concern about possible credit tightening; the ministry responded that the proposal was not designed to cause such tightening. This is the ministry's policy explanation, not proof of any future credit-market outcome.

MAFF opened consultation on 10 July 2026 and closed it on 8 August. Its results dated 18 September record eight submissions and state that the proposed ordinance would be adopted without substantive amendment in response to the submissions.

The final Cabinet Office–MAFF Ordinance No. 12 was promulgated on 18 September 2026 and commenced on 1 October 2026. The e-Gov revision record identifies a new Article 3-2 in the enforcement regulation. The ordinance's supplementary provision specifies commencement on that date without a separate transitional rule.

Under new Article 3-2(1), when the accounts for the specified guarantee operations show a year-end deficit, the institution may first draw down the reserve under Act Article 10(1). If a deficit remains, it may draw down the transfer-in amount under Article 10(2). Paragraph 2 separately permits that transfer-in amount to cover a deficit carried forward from the previous business year. The statutory Japanese uses できる, so the provision confers permission rather than requiring every institution to exhaust reserves automatically.

The order matters because it makes the accounting treatment of specified guarantee-business shortfalls explicit. It does not itself prescribe the price, availability or approval of agricultural loans, and it should not be confused with separate 2026 reforms to agricultural modernisation financing.

confirmed.text: Consultation on the draft ordinance opened.
Ordinance No. 12 was promulgated; MAFF published its consultation outcome.

expected: Guarantee institutions may need to align accounting procedures and audit evidence with the express reserve and transfer sequence, subject to the parent Act and their applicable accounting framework.
uncertainties: The amendment does not itself establish the amount of reserves available to any particular institution or prove that any deficit will be fully covered.
The consultation's suggestions about explanatory charts or procedural changes must not be treated as adopted legal requirements unless separately confirmed.
The parent Act Articles 10 and 11 and the complete consultation response still require independent final cross-check before this draft can be approved for publication.

paragraphs: Guarantee institutions should distinguish current-year shortfalls from amounts carried forward: the new paragraphs describe different permitted sources of coverage. The permission to draw down is not a requirement to transfer an unlimited amount, nor an entitlement for an individual farm borrower.

For agricultural lenders and their counterparties, the reform may support confidence in guarantee-system continuity, but it does not guarantee additional credit supply. The institution's balance sheet, statutory accounting and ordinary credit decisions remain relevant.
checklist: Identify whether the accounts concern guarantee operations listed in Act Article 11 items 1–3.
Determine whether the deficit arises in the current year or was carried forward from a prior business year.
For a current-year deficit, check the Article 10(1) reserve before considering the Article 10(2) transfer-in amount for any remaining shortfall.
Record accounting approvals and reserve balances; do not characterize the permissive provision as an automatic duty.
Verify the current parent Act and any administrative accounting guidance before finalizing institution-specific procedures.
